'''George Franklin Sterman''' (born June 2, 1946)<ref>{{cite book|title=Marquis Who's Who in Science and Engineering, 1st Edition|year=2001}}</ref> is an American theoretical physicist and the Director of the [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at [[Stony Brook University]] where he holds the rank Distinguished Professor.

==Background==
George Sterman received an A.B. from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1968. He earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Maryland]] in 1974,<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=133336}}</ref> and held research associate positions at the [[University of Illinois]] (1974–1976), [[Stony Brook University]] (1976–1978) and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (1978–1979), before joining the faculty of the C.N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics at Stony Brook in 1979. He became director of the Institute in 2001.<ref name="sakuri">{{cite web|title= 2003 J. J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=George%20Sterman&year=2003|publisher=APS|accessdate=5 September 2010}}</ref>

==Research==
George Sterman's research focuses on quantum field theory and its applications in [[quantum chromodynamics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=George Sterman Research profile|url=http://insti.physics.sunysb.edu/physics/forms/profilesearch.cgi?lastname=sterman|accessdate=5 September 2010|archive-date=15 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170615173833/http://insti.physics.sunysb.edu/physics/forms/profilesearch.cgi?lastname=sterman|url-status=dead}}</ref> With [[Steven Weinberg]] he proved the infrared finiteness of jet cross sections, thus proving that perturbation theory is a safe method in that regime.<ref name="sakuri"/>  He also worked on reformulation and proof of factorization theorems with [[Stephen Libby]], [[John C. Collins]] and [[Davison E. Soper]].<ref name="sakuri"/> He authored a textbook entitled ''An Introduction to Quantum Field Theory'' in 1993.<ref>{{cite book|last=Sterman|first=George|title=An introduction to quantum field theory |year=1993|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-32258-4|pages=590|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rB_wdTnfTmoC&q=George%20Sterman&pg=PP1}}</ref> As of 2010 he has over 190 papers listed as published on HEP-SPIRES.

George Sterman was awarded an honorary doctorate from the [[ETH Zurich]] in Switzerland in 2026 “For his groundbreaking theoretical research in particle physics, in particular the discovery of concepts and structures in quantum chromodynamics that serve as the basis for the theoretical interpretation of collision experiments and enable precise tests of the fundamental laws of nature in high-energy physics.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gasparino |first=Michael |date=2026-01-05 |title=George Sterman Awarded Honorary Doctorate at ETH Zurich |url=https://news.stonybrook.edu/university/distinguished-professor-george-sterman-awarded-honorary-doctorate-at-eth-zurich/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |language=en-US}}</ref> He was also awarded the 2003 [[Sakurai Prize|J.J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics]] "For developing concepts and techniques in QCD, such as infrared safety and factorization in hard processes, which permitted precise quantitative predictions and experimental tests, and thereby helped to establish QCD as the theory of the strong interactions."<ref name="sakuri"/>  He received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1985, is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and has served as an Associate Editor for ''Physical Review Letters''.<ref name="sakuri"/>
